stories.headline: Glen Hansard, Oscar-Winning ‘Once’ Musician, Dead at 56 - Rolling Stone
stories.summary: Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard, who achieved international fame in the 2007 drama 'Once,' has died in a motorcycle crash at the age of 56.
stories.why: Hansard's death at 56 reminds you that indie authenticity—winning an Oscar for a $150k Irish folk film—still matters more than algorithm optimization, and that era of artist-driven cinema feels increasingly distant.

stories.headline: Marjorie Taylor Greene Ties the Knot With Brian Glenn in Las Vegas - TMZ
stories.summary: Marjorie Taylor Greene is now officially off the market ... because she just got hitched to her fiancé Brian Glenn in Las Vegas!
stories.why: Not culturally significant; this is celebrity tabloid filler that signals nothing beyond personal gossip.

stories.headline: ‘Super Troopers’ at 25: A quarter-century of mustaches and maple syrup — and a new film - AP News
stories.summary: A quarter of a century is a long time for mustache rides and syrup binges, but “Super Troopers” has gotten a lot of mileage out of the simple joys of friends goofing around. The comedy troupe Broken…
stories.why: Super Troopers at 25 represents the last comedy era before algorithmic content killed the 'friends making stupid movies together' model—if you watched it in college, you're watching a cultural artifact of pre-streaming friendship humor.

stories.headline: Jared Leto Accused of Criminal Sexual Conduct by Four Women in BBC Documentary - Variety
stories.summary: In 'Jared Leto: Hollywood's Dark Secret,' four women accuse him of criminal sexual conduct, including one of statutory rape, when they were teenagers.
stories.why: Leto's documentary accusation matters because he's been untouchable despite rumors for decades; this signals that even A-list method actors now face real consequences, and the 'troubled genius' excuse finally expires.

stories.headline: BTS withdraw from Grammys, a month after Asian pop prize introduced - BBC
stories.summary: All seven members of the band post a statement online, saying they will boycott the 2027 ceremony.
stories.why: BTS withdrawing from the Grammys over a new 'Asian pop' category signals K-pop's leverage shifting—they're no longer seeking Western validation, which reshapes what mainstream music credibility even means.

stories.headline: Why Did Bryan Kohberger Murder 4 University of Idaho Students? Investigator Shares Chilling Possible Theory - Oxygen Official Site
stories.summary: Find out more about one investigators theory on Bryan Kohberger's possible motive in murders of four University of Idaho college students.
stories.why: True crime obsession over a college murder case reveals how we've normalized parsing killers' psychology as entertainment; this content exists because the case already saturated your feed and feeds parasocial investment in tragedy.

stories.headline: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Swings to China’s Biggest Superhero Opening in Seven Years - The Hollywood Reporter
stories.summary: The film is set to earn more than $35 million on its first day in China, with local analysts projecting a full-run total as massive as $250 million.
stories.why: China's $250M Spider-Man opening signals that Marvel's real audience is now Asian markets, not you—Hollywood's profitability increasingly depends on plots and casts that resonate there first, fundamentally shifting what gets made.
